title: Pyramid Texts of Unas: Utterances 199, 32, 23, 25 and 200 (passage, north wall)
source: Pyramid of Unas, Saqqara, passage between sarcophagus chamber and antechamber, north wall (photograph: L. F. Husson for A. Piankoff 1968, via Pyramid Texts Online) + TLA transliteration (ed. D. Topmann, CC BY-SA 4.0) + English of S. A. B. Mercer (1952, public domain in the US)
description: The Pyramid Texts on the north wall of the passage between sarcophagus chamber and antechamber in the pyramid of Unas (c. 2350 BCE), utterance by utterance, with the TLA transliteration and Mercer's English.
introduction:
The Pyramid Texts are the oldest large body of Egyptian religious writing: spells, called utterances, for the resurrection of the dead king, his protection, his meals and his ascent to the sky, cut in vertical columns of hieroglyphs on the walls of the burial apartments of late Old Kingdom pyramids. The pyramid of Unas at Saqqara, the last king of the 5th Dynasty (about 2375-2345 BCE), is the first to carry them. Its sarcophagus chamber, the passage to the antechamber, the antechamber and the corridor hold 649 numbered columns of text; this library gives every column, wall by wall, in seventeen entries (227 different utterances, some of them inscribed more than once).

This entry is the north wall of the passage between sarcophagus chamber and antechamber: 19 columns of hieroglyphs, Sethe's W 341-359, which follow each other from the left-hand (west) edge of the photograph. It holds the utterances 199, 32, 23, 25, 200.

Each section is one utterance. The Egyptian is the transliteration of the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (edition by Doris Topmann), with Sethe's Unas column number (W) before each column; a number ending in 'a' marks the offering label at the foot of a column. Signs restored by the editor are in square brackets, signs the scribe left out in angle brackets, damaged signs in half brackets. The English is Samuel A. B. Mercer's translation of 1952. Mercer translates Sethe's composite text made from all the pyramids that have an utterance, so his wording can include clauses that are not in the Unas copy, and his section numbers (134a, 134b ...) are Sethe's paragraph numbers, not column numbers; he writes 'N.' where the wall has the king's name. The photograph shows the whole wall; each section's note gives its columns counted from the edge where the text on that wall begins.
translator_notes: Mercer's separate headings, postscripts and variants taken from other pyramids are left out.
Letters follow the sacred-texts transcription of Mercer: ȝ stands for aleph and ‘ for ayin; letters underlined in the printed book are given as ḏ, ṯ, ẖ.
Sethe's section numbers are kept as printed in that transcription, including a few misprints (for example '146.' for 141b in Utterance 215).
The TLA has no hieroglyphic encoding for these texts, so only the transliteration is shown.

translation.text:
115aTo say: O Osiris N., turn thyself towards this thy bread;
115breceive it from (my) hand. To say four times: May the eye of Horus flourish (?) for thee.
115cA wḏb offering-which-the-god-gives of bread, cake and liquid.
translation.scan_note: Unas W 341-342: W 341-342 are columns 1-2 of the 19 columns on the photograph of the passage, north wall, counted from the left-hand (west) edge. Wall check (north wall): 19 columns (partial ones at both edges), W 341 at the left-hand (west) edge to W 359 at the right. Checked on the image: the repeated kꜣ arms of PT 25 fill the 11th and 12th columns from the left (W 351-352); the cartouche is low in the 7th column (W 347) and high in the 9th (W 349), as in the text. Mercer's English renders Sethe's composite text of this utterance from all pyramids; it can contain words that are not in the Unas copy.

translation.text:
22aThis is thy cool water, Osiris; this is thy cool water, O N., which went forth from thy son, which went forth from Horus.
22bI have come; I have brought to thee the eye of Horus, that thy heart may be refreshed by it. I have brought it to thee. It is under thy soles.
23aTake to thyself the efflux (sweat), which goes forth from thee; thy heart shall not be weary thereby.
23bTo say four times, when thou goest forth justified: Libation; two pellets of natron.

translation.text:
16aOsiris, carry off all those who hate N., who speak evilly against his name.
16bThot, go, carry off him who has injured Osiris. Bring him who speaks evilly against the name of N.
16cGet him into thy hand. To say four times: Do not separate thyself from him.
16dTake care that thou be not separated from him. A libation.

translation.text:
17aHe who goes, goes with his ka: Horus goes with his ka; Set goes with his ka;
17bThot goes with his ka; the god goes with his ka; Osiris goes with his ka;
17cMḫnti-’irti goes with his ka; thou also goest with thy ka.
18aO N., the hands of thy ka are before thee; O N., the hands of thy ka are behind thee;
18bO N., the feet of thy ka are before thee; O N., the feet of thy ka are behind thee.
18cOsiris N., I have given to thee the eye of Horus, so that thy face may be equipped with it.
18dLet the odour of the eye of Horus adhere to thee. To be said four times: Fire of incense.

translation.text:
116aHomage to thee, Incense; greetings to thee, Divine Brother; greetings to thee mnwr (incense), in the limbs of Horus.
116bBe great, my father; propagate thyself in thy name of pȝḏ (pellet of incense).
116cThine odour is for N.; thy perfume is f or N.
116dEye of Horus, thou art higher, thou art greater than N. Incense.
